label: behavior_log plugin: log-observation + behavior-summary
origin: User insight: a single external observation of instance behavior is an unverified claim (kernel Sec 9), but a TIME SERIES of observations becomes checkable for consistency, recurrence, and drift in the observing method itself -- different epistemic status than one-shot verification.
explicit_limit_preserved: Consistency is not accuracy -- a biased observer produces a large, stable, still-wrong dataset. behavior-summary states this directly in its own output, not just in the docstring, so the caveat travels with the tool, not just the code comment.
design: log-observation records subject/category/severity/description/observer/verified-flag as a behavioral_observation ledger event. behavior-summary aggregates: verified-vs-unverified ratio, by-category, by-severity, by-subject (recurrence), by-observer (cross-observer agreement is flagged as the real consistency signal, single-observer consistency is flagged as weaker).
tested_with: Real seed data describing this sessions actual ReSSERAct fabrication incident (verified=true, I confirmed via search) plus one unverified speculative entry -- confirmed the tool correctly surfaces the verified/unverified split and recurrence rather than just counting.

change: Sec 9 Cross-Model Provenance: added Turning the risk into a process paragraph after the existing fresh-pass test. Converts repeated agreement is not verification from a pure warning into a directive to actively cross-examine convergent claims against a diverse independent source (direct search, actual file, primary document) -- formalizes a practice already used organically all session (verifying ChatGPT/Gemini claims via real search, e.g. ReSSERAct, GPT-5.6/Gemini-3.6-Flash model name checks).

label: ledger-compact: recursive skeleton-of-skeletons rollup (second tier)
origin: User correctly identified a real scaling gap: skeleton summaries themselves were never re-compacted, meaning skeleton count could grow unbounded over a very long project life. Verified this is NOT novel research -- confirmed via search as a well-established pattern (hierarchical/tiered rollups, standard in time-series databases like TimescaleDB/InfluxDB), applied here to a new domain (structured event logs).
design: compact_ledger now takes keep_skeletons (default 10). Once plain skeleton count exceeds it, oldest skeletons roll into ONE meta-skeleton (aggregated entries_summarized, event-type counts, earliest period, capped label sample). If a meta-skeleton already exists, MERGES into it rather than creating a second one.
real_bug_found_by_own_test: First implementation appended a NEW meta-skeleton on every rollup instead of merging into an existing one -- meta-skeletons would have accumulated unboundedly, exactly the problem this tier exists to prevent. Caught by test_meta_skeleton_itself_is_never_rolled_up_again (idempotence check, called compact_ledger twice), fixed to merge into existing meta-skeleton.
tested_with: 4 new tests: below-threshold no-op, correct rollup math (raw_entries_covered and by_event_type sums verified exactly), meta-skeleton merge/idempotence, both tiers firing together in one call. Also ran against the real growth_ledger.jsonl (genuinely compacted -- 44 raw entries had exceeded threshold).

label: behavior_log: provenance-diversity check (source contamination vs independence)
origin: ChatGPT calibrated audit, verified against actual kernel text before acting (A7 wording and A3 relay-provenance clause both confirmed accurate, not paraphrased). Core insight: agreeing observations are only real independent verification if they trace to genuinely different sources -- multiple observers citing the SAME underlying source is contamination wearing agreements clothes, not evidence.
design: log-observation gains optional --source flag (URL, file path, dataset). behavior-summary groups observations by subject/category and reports: no sources cited (cant check independence), same source cited by all (flagged as likely contamination), or multiple distinct sources cited (flagged as genuine provenance diversity).
tested_with: Deliberate synthetic test cases -- one shared-source pair (correctly flagged as contamination), one distinct-source pair (correctly flagged as genuine diversity), confirmed against real pre-existing sourceless entries (correctly flagged as unable to check). Test entries removed from the ledger after verification, real seed data (ReSSERAct etc.) left intact.

label: relay_console: structural home for provenance metadata (Turn.evidence_tier, Turn.provenance_note)
origin: ChatGPT audit 4 finding: relay currently transports plain text, no structural place for A3 evidence tiers to live during a relay hop -- protocol SAYS preserve provenance, nothing enforces or even offers a place for it. Closed directly per user request, not deferred.
design: Turn model gains optional evidence_tier (V/I/A/U) and provenance_note fields. Async paste-bar UI gains two optional fields so a human relaying content can tag what theyre pasting. Direct API-call turns (sync modes) get None for both -- not fabricated, honestly absent since the model itself didnt supply them structurally. Transcript display shows the tags when present.
scope_honesty: This gives provenance a real place to live -- it does NOT auto-extract tags from freeform model text (that would be its own unreliable inference problem, ironic given the topic). Populating these fields requires a human or a future structured-output integration to actually supply them.

Could not run a full pydantic-based import test -- relay_console was never pip-installed in this sandbox (no network access to install pydantic here). Verified the exact asyncio.Future 4-tuple unpacking pattern used in submit_paste/_wait_for_human_paste/submit_gate_action directly instead, confirmed correct. label: relay_console: no timeout on provider API calls, unbounded context growth unobserved
origin: Reasoned through Gemini audit 1 directly rather than accepting its framing. 2 of its 5 findings (dependency-aware orchestration, over-decomposition thresholds) describe parallel sub-agent architecture -- relay_console is strictly sequential round-robin, those failure modes cannot occur here, not real gaps for this architecture. Verified the other 2 (context cost floor, router fallback) directly against actual code instead: found neither timeout nor context-growth visibility existed, confirmed via grep (zero timeout matches) and reading _history_for (unbounded, full history sent every turn).
fixes: call_provider wrapped in asyncio.wait_for(90s) -- a hung API call previously could stall the entire relay indefinitely with no recovery, matching Jaidev article finding about an orchestrator with no fallback. Tested the asyncio.wait_for timeout pattern directly (real async test, not just syntax check).

Turn history >20 messages now logs a visible warning -- deliberately NOT auto-truncated, since silently cutting relay history risks breaking coherence, a worse failure than visible unbounded growth. Makes the growth observable instead of silent.
not_built_and_why: Dependency-envelope locking and decomposition-threshold gating -- both describe a parallel multi-worker architecture relay_console does not have and was not asked to become. Building locks for dependencies that cannot exist in a strictly sequential design would be solving a problem this architecture does not have.

label: relay_console: THE actual root cause found -- session.start() awaited inline, deadlocking the message-receive loop
origin: Extended live debugging session: JS sync errors, promise rejections, WebSocket lifecycle all ruled out via on-page debug panel. Network monitoring panel (built mid-session) proved submit_paste and stop were both genuinely SENT successfully from the browser. TRACE prints with flush=True still never fired for either. That combination -- confirmed sent, zero server-side effect, for two different actions -- pointed at something structural rather than an action-specific bug.
root_cause: main.py relay_ws():  was called directly inside the same while True loop that receives ALL subsequent WebSocket messages (submit_paste, stop, gate_action). session.start() internally blocks on _wait_for_human_paste(), which can only resolve via a LATER submit_paste message -- but the loop can never reach websocket.receive_json() again to get that message, because it is still awaiting start() on the line above. Genuine deadlock: start() waits for a message the loop cannot receive because it is waiting for start().
why_every_diagnostic_came_back_clean: The browser-side send always succeeds (TCP-level, independent of whether anything ever reads it). The specific line of code that would have printed a TRACE message, or done anything at all with submit_paste, was never reached -- not skipped due to an exception, literally never executed, because control flow never returned to that branch of the loop.
fix: session.start() is now scheduled via asyncio.create_task() instead of awaited inline, letting the outer receive loop continue processing subsequent messages concurrently. Task reference kept in a new BACKGROUND_TASKS dict to prevent garbage collection mid-flight (asyncio best practice for fire-and-forget tasks).
verified_with: Direct, standalone async reproduction (no pydantic needed) proving the OLD pattern deadlocks under asyncio.wait_for(timeout=1.0) exactly as diagnosed, and the NEW pattern (create_task) completes successfully with the correct value. Full 35-test suite and secret scan also pass.

label: sandbox_runner: fixed real cross-environment memory-limit portability regression found by independent ChatGPT execution audit
origin: ChatGPT independently executed v0.8.0-alpha and reported 50/56, with 2 sandbox test failures under SIGKILL at 128MB despite the CLI default already being 256MB. Investigated directly: RLIMIT_AS constrains virtual address space, not actual usage -- confirmed my own environments baseline Python VmSize (~16MB) is comfortably under 128MB, explaining why it passed here, while a different Python build/OS/libc could plausibly need more just for interpreter startup, independent of script content.
fix: Raised the should-succeed tests from memory_mb=128 to 512, and the CLI default from 256 to 512 -- the actual memory-boundary test (memory_mb=32, expects a real MemoryError) deliberately left tight, since thats what it exists to test.
tested_with: Full sandbox_runner test file re-run after the fix: MemoryError boundary test still correctly triggers at 32MB, all should-succeed tests pass with real headroom. 56/56 full suite.

Could not reproduce or diagnose why their environment produced a FAIL rather than the expected clean SKIP from the existing code as written. Asked ChatGPT for more detail rather than guessing at a fix for something unreproduced here.

label: Fixed session_close preflight check testing the wrong property -- diagnosed precisely by independent ChatGPT audit
origin: ChatGPT precisely diagnosed the real mechanism: setUp checked import from the test runners own CWD (project root), which finds the source tree on sys.path even when llmos_toolkit genuinely isnt pip-installed -- but the real test runs with cwd=self.root (a disposable temp dir with no source tree in sight), so the check was testing a different, easier property than what the actual test needed. Verified directly before applying: confirmed in my environment a genuinely-installed package imports identically with or without the cwd override, so the fix is safe here and correctly reveals the gap in a different environment.
fix: setUp now creates self.root FIRST, then runs the import check WITH cwd=self.root, matching the real tests actual conditions exactly. Also fixed a correctness wrinkle the reorder introduced: switched from tearDown to addCleanup for the temp dir, since tearDown does not run if setUp raises (including via skipTest) -- addCleanup does, so the skip case now cleans up properly too, not just left for eventual GC. Removed the now-redundant tearDown.
tested_with: Full test file re-run: all 4 tests still pass genuinely in this environment (real install, so check still passes cleanly, just faithfully now). Full 56-test suite confirmed clean.
